resale_co.how_to_apply: Nothing to apply for from the Township for a resale of a home. The Township's Community Development and Planning page says a certificate of occupancy from the construction office is not required for re-sales and tells sellers to get the smoke detector certification from the local fire district (see fire certificate). The rental certificate of compliance (Chapter 59A) applies only when a rental unit changes tenants.

resale_co.notes: Re-checked 2026-10-20. New this check: the Township's Community Development and Planning page (posted September 10, 2026) now says in writing that a certificate of occupancy from the construction office is not required for re-sales of homes, and lists the six fire districts to call for the smoke detector certification. That settles the status as not required with high confidence. It matches what the code showed last week (read through the ecode360 print view, Township of Gloucester code GL0340): Chapter 42 'Certificates of Occupancy' only covers new homes in major subdivisions; Chapter 59A requires a certificate of rental housing and property maintenance compliance each time a rental unit changes tenants (a rental program, not a resale requirement); Chapter 59 (Housing Code) and Chapter 67A (Property Maintenance) have no sale provision; and neither fee chapter (Chapter 51, Chapter A201) lists a resale fee. The 'Application for a Certificate of Occupancy' on the page is the state construction CO form (UCC F270) for permitted work. The fire district phone list on that page differs from the district sites in places: District #2 856-939-2090 (the district's own page gives 856-282-3370 ext. 124), District #3 Blenheim 856-227-0552, District #4 856-227-7731 (the district's page gives 856-227-7037). The ordinance lead URL in the town pack points to Gloucester City, not Gloucester Township.

requirements: Districts 1, 2, 4 and 5: CO alarms must be less than 7 years old

Districts 1, 4 and 5: smoke alarms older than 10 years not accepted; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed (hardwired exempt); hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms. District 6: hardwired units more than 10 years old must be replaced
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell on the ceiling (not between joists); hallway alarms within 10 feet of all bedroom doors
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently on the house and visible from the street (mailbox or light post numbers not accepted)

Homes with a secondary power source (solar, generator, battery storage) need a non-handwritten 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER' label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter

District 5 checklist: alarm type follows the year the house was built (for example 1991 to present: hardwired interconnected alarms with battery backup on every level and in each bedroom); hardwired fire alarm systems need an NFPA 72 test report at the inspection
Current district forms do not list a fire extinguisher (District 6's 2026 affidavit title still says 'Portable Fire Extinguisher' but its checklist has no extinguisher item)

fire_cert.notes: Gloucester Township has six fire districts, and the right one depends on the address: look up the property on the Township's Edmunds page (https://wipp.edmundsassoc.com/Wipp/?wippid=0415); the fire district appears in the 'Special Taxing Districts' block. The Township's Community Development page (September 2026) also lists a phone number for each district. District 3 (Blenheim) has no local fire code enforcing agency; the NJ DCA Division of Fire Safety issues smoke certificates there (DCA registry code 'S', and DCA's state-enforced towns list marks it 'SC = Smoke Certs'). Fees differ by district: Districts 2 and 6 charge $35/$70/$125; Districts 1, 4 and 5 and DCA charge $45/$90/$161. Re-checked 2026-10-20: all six district forms are the same files as last week and the fees are unchanged. District 2's application is a Word file (.docx, updated 4/16/2025); its fee rows were re-read by hand from the file text on 2026-10-20 and are unchanged, but an automatic check that reads the raw .docx bytes cannot find them, so a 'not found' result on those three District 2 fees means the checker could not read the file, not that the fees changed. District 2 has no PDF or web-page copy of its fee table. District 2 also posts a 'CO Information Sheet' (Word file) with placement rules. District 5's form is a one-page scan; its fees were read by eye on 2026-10-20 and are unchanged. District 5's page also links 'Smoke Pass Fail' (Smoke42025.pdf), which returns a 404. District 1's site resets plain downloads but its forms page still links the 08-2025 application; its Fire Marshall page names Harry D. Woods. The DCA fire directory lists District 5 fire official email sschwegel@lambsfire.com and District 6 fire official James Gordon, Sr (jgordon6231@yahoo.com, a personal address, not added); the district sites do not show these emails. The Township website also hosts an outdated District 1 form from 2014 (https://glotwp.com/downloads/General/District1.pdf, $35/$70/$125 with an extinguisher requirement); District 1's own current form is dated 08-2025.

open_questions: Exact street boundaries of each fire district are not published; use the Edmunds property lookup.
District 2 and District 6 forms do not state a re-inspection fee.
District 3's own website (gtfd3.com, redirecting to blenheimfire.com) is behind a captcha and could not be read; DCA handles its smoke certificates.
Phone numbers for Districts 2 and 4 on the Township page differ from the districts' own pages; use the district pages.
